newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Q3 cocoa grind up 7.52 pct, to 93,933 tonnes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Q3 cocoa grind up 7.52 pct, to 93,933 tonnes.

text.p: U.S. third quarter grindings increased 7.52 percent compared to the same year-ago period to 93,933 tonnes, floor souces said.
The percentage change on grindings reflects a revised third-quarter 1995 total of 87,360 tonnes, they said. The figure had initially been reported at a record high of 94,485 tonnes.
The quantity of liquor melted rose by 1.4 percent versus third-quarter 1995 levels, to 19,042 tonnes, while total butter melted was down 6.8 percent, to 16,757 tonnes.

Traders said the grind figures -- which represent the amount of cocoa processed by U.S. manufacturers -- were mainly neutral. But some traders said the number was toward the high end of expectations and could buoy CSCE cocoa prices.
Analysts' forecasts had ranged from between three and ten percent higher, with the majority calling for an increase toward the lower end of the range.
"With the revision it is a new record for the most cocoa ever ground in the U.S.," one trader said. "I consider it positive and in line with robust growth in Europe."
But other traders said after posting gains the past three consecutive sessions, the grinds' rise was well anticipated by the market.
"I think there was some buying in the market yesterday in anticipation of the news," one trader said.

The rise in the U.S. figures confirmed the steady upward trend in cocoa consumption worldwide, traders and analysts said. But after strong third-quarter grinds in Europe, some operators said the market's reaction to the U.S. figures was likely to be muted.
"The bulk of the information is already out there after the European grinds," said Prudential Securities analyst Arthur Stevenson. "After their release the impact of the U.S. grind is diluted."

The Dutch third quarter grind rose by 16.69 percent versus the same quarter last year, to 99,549 tonnes, while the U.K. grind jumped 42 percent in the third quarter to 48,855 tonnes. Last quarter's German grind was up a more modest seven percent, to 65,824 tonnes, but it still surpassed analysts' expectations.
